predecessors.name: British Africa (remaining colonies)
predecessors.text: the Uganda Protectorate, held in Cliopatria's British East Africa shape (1961-1968) with Kenya, Rhodesia, Nyasaland, Basutoland and others

ledger.x: 9 October 1962: Uganda becomes independent of the United Kingdom as a dominion, with Milton Obote as the first prime minister.
9 October 1963: Uganda is declared a republic (infobox 'Republic declared: 9 October 1963').
30 October 1978: Uganda invades the Kagera Salient of Tanzania.
Early January 1979: the last Ugandan troops leave Kagera.
20-21 January 1979: Tanzanian troops cross into Uganda.
11 April 1979: Kampala falls and Amin's rule ends.
April 1979: Tanzanian forces hold Uganda behind the new UNLF government.
August 1998: the Second Congo War opens and Uganda holds the north and north-east of the Congo.
7 August 1999: the Ugandan and Rwandan armies fight in Kisangani.
17 August 1999: a ceasefire halts the first Kisangani fighting.
May 2000: Uganda and Rwanda fight again in Kisangani: 'heavy fighting between Uganda and Rwanda in Kisangani in May and June 2000'.
June 2000: the second Kisangani fighting ends (the page says only 'in May and June 2000'; June is the last month it names).
6 September 2002: the Luanda Agreement 'formalised peace between Congo and Uganda'; the year is that of the section it stands in.

wars.name: Uganda–Tanzania War
wars.outcome: Tanzanian victory: the Kagera Salient was cleared by early January 1979, Kampala fell on 11 April 1979 and Amin fled; the infobox gives '9 October 1978 – 3 June 1979' and 'Collapse of the Second Republic of Uganda'.

wars.name: Second Congo War
wars.outcome: The Luanda Agreement of 6 September 2002 'formalised peace between Congo and Uganda'; the war 'officially ended on 18 July 2003 with the establishment of the Transitional Government'.

certainty.note: Inherited colonial boundaries; the page records no change or dispute after 1962 (Lake Victoria, the Victoria Nile and Lake Albert are natural lines).
